title: Rash with Joint Pain
hpi_narrative: {{patient_name}} presents with malar (butterfly) rash across cheeks (sparing nasolabial folds), photosensitivity, polyarthritis, fatigue, and fever. SLE is a multisystem autoimmune disease with autoantibodies against nuclear antigens. Diagnosis per ACR/EULAR criteria: ANA positivity is required (sensitive but not specific). Anti-dsDNA and anti-Smith are specific for SLE. Other features: oral ulcers, serositis (pleuritis/pericarditis), nephritis (proteinuria, RBC casts), neurologic (seizures/psychosis), hematologic (anemia, leukopenia, lymphopenia, thrombocytopenia). Monitor: CBC, BMP, UA (proteinuria), complement C3/C4 (low = active disease), anti-dsDNA titers (correlates with disease activity). Treatment: mild (skin/joints) → hydroxychloroquine (ALL SLE patients) + NSAIDs. Moderate: add steroids (prednisone). Severe (nephritis, CNS) → high-dose steroids + immunosuppression (mycophenolate mofetil or cyclophosphamide). Sun protection.

stacks.label: Hydroxychloroquine
stacks.finding: All SLE patients. Reduces flares and mortality.

stacks.label: Prednisone (if moderate/severe)
stacks.finding: For flares. Taper to lowest effective dose.
